items.title: The family consisting of $H_5$ and co-$E$ has the Erdős–Hajnal property
items.strategy: Use the Erdős–Hajnal property of $H_0$ and of $\overline{P_5}$ to obtain the two base forbidden families by hereditary-subclass monotonicity. For each $i=1,\ldots,5$, apply Huang--Ju--Zhou Corollary 1.8 directly to $\{H_i,\mathrm{co}	ext{-}E\}$: deleting the chosen leaf of $H_i$ gives $H_{i-1}$, while deleting the chosen co-leaf of co-$E$ gives $\overline{P_5}$. Induct on $i$.

items.title: The special-vertex-local structural-partition criterion implies property (*)
items.strategy: Fix only an arbitrary special-vertex comb and its supplied partition. Prove directly the large-Y outcome and the two-sided external-purity transversal alternative, then reorder one small-block partition of X with |X|>w/2. Establish nonempty integral layers and m_r>=ell^(r/4) for r<q by the floor inequality. Apply the common EH constant to the induced pattern on the first m_r blocks and lift its clique/stable set directly, obtaining c1=c3=c/4 and c2=10/c. If no layer is wide, sum all layers, including the terminal layer, to obtain |X|<23w/60<w/2. Do not invoke any universally quantified structural-partition lemma.

items.title: Relative to a complete nonedge pair in a co-$E$-free graph, a one-sided vertex mixed on an induced path avoids two consecutive nonneighbours and three consecutive neighbours
items.strategy: Fix an induced path $P$, nonadjacent vertices $x,y$ outside $P$ that are complete to $P$, and a vertex $u\in N(x)\setminus N(y)$ mixed on $P$. Two consecutive nonneighbours of $u$, together with the preceding adjacency change, give an induced subpath $a-b-c$ for which $\{x,y,u,a,b,c\}$ induces co-$E$. Three consecutive neighbours followed by a nonneighbour give an induced subpath $a-b-c-d$ for which $\{y,u,a,b,c,d\}$ induces co-$E$. Verify all nonedges, not merely the displayed path edges.

items.title: Relative to a complete nonedge pair in a co-$E$-free graph, every one-sided vertex is pure to an induced $H_5$
items.strategy: Fix nonadjacent vertices $x,y$ complete to an induced $H_5$ and a vertex $u\in N(x)\setminus N(y)$. Apply the preceding path-run obstruction to the labeled rim, rim-leaf, and hub paths. Treat separately the cases in which $u$ is complete to the rim, anticomplete to the rim, or mixed on it; each case forces either purity or an explicit co-$E$ contradiction. Then record the source's comb specialization with $(x,y)=(v,a_i)$.

items.title: The $H_5$-overlap-chain relation in one comb block
Every $H_5$-overlap class is connected
items.strategy: A chain of induced $H_5$ copies links any two of its vertices through successive copies sharing a vertex. Each $H_5$ is connected, so concatenate paths inside the copies; this also records why the initial overlap classes meet the connected-block hypothesis for quotienting.

items.title: Purity on every induced $H_5$ propagates along an $H_5$-overlap class
items.strategy: Two induced $H_5$ copies meeting in a vertex cannot receive opposite complete/anticomplete labels from one external vertex, because their common vertex would then have both adjacencies. Induct along an overlap chain to give one common label on the whole class.

items.title: The $H_5$-overlap blockade and its iterated mixed quotients
Iterated mixed quotients of an $H_5$-overlap blockade terminate at a pure blockade
items.strategy: If a finite blockade is not pure, two distinct blocks are mixed and their mixed-reachability class has at least two blocks, so quotienting strictly decreases the number of blocks. Apply well-ordering to this strictly decreasing positive-integer measure; the first fixed quotient has no mixed pair and hence is pure.

items.title: A vertex mixed on a connected set has opposite adjacency on some edge of that set
items.strategy: Choose a neighbour and a nonneighbour of the external vertex in the connected induced subgraph. Along a path between them, the first change in its adjacency to the external vertex occurs across an edge, which is the required mixed edge.

items.title: In a special-vertex comb of a co-$E$-free graph, vertices in other comb blocks remain pure to every $H_5$-overlap quotient block
items.strategy: Assume the comb has a vertex $v$ complete to all blocks and anticomplete to all teeth. Induct over the overlap blockade and its quotient iterates, beginning with the complete nonedge pair $(v,a_i)$. A mixed external vertex on a new quotient block yields opposite member blocks by the quotient lemma. Their connectedness turns any prohibited cross mixedness into a mixed edge, which violates the path-run obstruction; repeatedly descend the quotient witness to two initial overlap classes, then use $H_5$ homogeneity and overlap-chain purity to obtain the final contradiction.

items.title: The pattern of the terminal $H_5$-overlap quotient is $\{H_5,\mathrm{co}\text{-}E\}$-free
items.strategy: An induced $H_5$ in the pattern would lift through the pure terminal blocks to an induced $H_5$ of the ambient graph whose vertices lie in distinct terminal blocks, contradicting that each source $H_5$ begins within one overlap class and quotienting only merges classes. An induced co-$E$ in the pattern similarly lifts through pairwise pure blocks to an induced co-$E$ in the ambient graph.

items.title: A special-vertex comb in a co-$E$-free graph admits the $\{H_5,\mathrm{co}\text{-}E\}$ structural partition
items.strategy: Fix a co-$E$-free graph with a comb and a vertex $v$ outside the comb that is complete to all blocks and anticomplete to all teeth, as in source Lemma 6.4. In each comb block, let $X_i$ be the vertices contained in an induced $H_5$ and let $Y_i$ be the complement. If $X_i$ is nonempty, its overlap blockade terminates at a pure quotient; the terminal-pattern lemma gives its $\{H_5,\mathrm{co}\text{-}E\}$-freeness, while the special-vertex external-purity lemma gives the cross-block condition. If $X_i$ is empty, move one vertex of the nonempty block $B_i$ from $Y_i$ to $X_i$; the resulting singleton blockade is pure with a one-vertex pattern, and every outside vertex is automatically pure to its singleton block. In both cases $Y_i$ is $H_5$-free by construction and co-$E$-free as an induced subgraph of $G$.

items.title: The singleton family $\{E\}$ has property (*)
items.strategy: Apply the special-vertex-local criterion with $\mathcal F_1=\mathcal F_2=\{H_5,\mathrm{co}\text{-}E\}$ and $\mathcal H=\{E\}$. The batch's Erdős–Hajnal lemma supplies the common constant. For an arbitrary special-vertex comb in an $\overline{\mathcal H}=\{\mathrm{co}\text{-}E\}$-free graph, the exact special-vertex structural theorem supplies the required partition. The local criterion then gives property (*) for $\{E\}$. This application deliberately does not assert that Lemma 6.4 supplies the universal hypothesis of the published structural criterion.

title: Comb Structure in co-E-Free Graphs — Examples

items.title: The two induced co-$E$ witnesses behind the forbidden path runs
items.strategy: Give the two six-vertex adjacency tables from Claim 6.4.1: one with a mixed vertex followed by two consecutive nonneighbours on a three-vertex path, and one with three consecutive neighbours followed by a nonneighbour on a four-vertex path. Complement the listed $E$-edges and check every remaining pair, so the drawings do not hide an unwanted chord.

items.title: An $H_5$-overlap class and its terminal quotient
items.strategy: Fix a comb block whose induced graph consists of two induced $H_5$ copies sharing one labeled rim vertex. Verify the shared vertex makes all displayed vertices one overlap class, check connectedness from the two copies, and observe that the resulting one-block blockade is already pure; this is a finite adjacency-data check of the initial and terminal constructions.

items.title: A bipartite four-tooth comb has the co-$E$ structural partition
items.strategy: Take four independent four-vertex blocks, one tooth complete only to each corresponding block, and one additional vertex complete to all blocks and anticomplete to the teeth. Verify from the full bipartition that the graph is co-$E$-free because co-$E$ contains a triangle. In each $B_i$, choose one vertex $x_i$, put $X_i=\{x_i\}$ and $Y_i=B_i\setminus\{x_i\}$, and check directly that the singleton blockade, its one-vertex pattern, the $H_5$-free remainder, and all cross-block purity clauses satisfy the structural partition.
